jobs.description:
Petrolink Support is looking for 2 experienced Subsea Facilities Structures & Manifolds and tie in Lead Engineers to follow-up the planning, engineering, fabrication and delivery of subsea structures and manifolds in and/or the the tie in for our client.

Contract location: Stavanger / Oslo

Tasks
Typical work tasks will be 

• Follow up the execution of the Subsea Facilities Structures and Manifolds and/or tie in scope of work, including planning, detail engineering, documentation, fabrication, and delivery activities.

• Monitor HSE, quality, progress, and execution performance.

• Provide independent assurance that project requirements, including client's technical requirements, are being implemented.

• Identify and drive interfaces with key project disciplines, and ensure integration between subsea areas through interface management and change management.

• Identify, communicate, and support resolution of technical, quality, schedule, and execution risks.

• Deliver regular reporting to the client's project team on progress, key issues, and opportunities. Provide evaluations, reports and presentations as required for key project milestones.

• Engineering degree or equivalent technical qualification.

• Minimum 10 years' experience within offshore subsea projects.

• Experience with engineering of subsea structures, manifolds or templates, tie in.

• Experience working with EPC/EPCI contractors and fabrication yards.

• Knowledge of NORSOK, DNV, API, and offshore industry standards is desirable.

• Strong communication, stakeholder management, and leadership skills.

• Fluent in written and spoken English and Norwegian

• Experience from the Norwegian oil & gas industry.
Personal qualities
We are looking for people with the following qualities:

• Team player, strong collaboration and communication skills.

• Ability to deliver results.

• Structured and systematic.

• High focus on Sustainability, Ethics and Company values.
We offer

• Good insurance schemes.

• Exciting projects and challenges.

jobs.description:
Secondary Engineer -- Control and Protection

Oslo, Norway

12-month renewable contract

Grid Protection Client

About the company

Applica are partnering with a leading international provider of technology and engineering solutions for the energy and power sectors, specialising in high-voltage substations, power systems and transmission infrastructure. With an established international engineering network, they deliver projects supporting the development and reliability of energy infrastructure.

About the role

You will be an experienced Secondary Engineer specialising in Control & Protection to support the delivery of high-voltage substation projects across Norway.

You will take responsibility for the engineering and coordination of Control & Protection packages, ensuring designs are technically compliant, complete and delivered to the required standards.

Key responsibilities include:

• 

Leading and coordinating Control & Protection engineering activities, including sub-suppliers.

• 

Delivering technical designs, calculations and documentation from base design through to detailed design and as-built documentation.

• 

Producing technical drawings, specifications and project procedures.

• 

Providing technical recommendations and resolving engineering queries throughout project delivery.

• 

Supporting project planning, resource estimates, risk assessments and technical proposals.

• 

Working closely with project teams, factories and suppliers across Europe.

• 

Providing technical support during installation, testing and commissioning activities.

• 

Ensuring compliance with customer requirements, relevant standards and safety regulations.

About you

To be successful in this role, you will have:

• 

A Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering or a similar discipline.

• 

A minimum of 5 years' experience within an engineering department or on-site engineering environment.

• 

Strong technical knowledge of substation Control & Protection engineering and project execution.

• 

The ability to coordinate engineering activities and work effectively with suppliers and multidisciplinary teams.

• 

Fluency in both written and spoken Norwegian and English.

The following experience would also be advantageous:

• 

Electrical design software such as EPLAN, E3 or AutoCAD.

• 

Knowledge of power systems, renewable energy and transmission systems.

• 

Experience with control systems, SCADA and programming.

• 

Familiarity with IED tools such as PCM600.

• 

Knowledge of Norwegian power system legislation and standards.

• 

Experience with protection testing, commissioning and secondary and primary injection testing.

New company

Join the future of Sustainable Manufacturing at reTyre!
At reTyre, you’re not just joining a company — you’re joining a groundbreaking industrial journey together with a great team of innovators.

We’ve built the world’s first sustainable tire factory, right in the heart of Ski, 20 min outside of Oslo.

We are now looking for a skilled Senior Industrialization Engineer to join the Manufacturing team and drive our mission forward. Our factory uses a revolutionary production method that makes it possible to replace traditional rubber in pneumatic tires with new, sustainable materials.

Our team is internationally diverse, young, energetic, and united by a passion for innovation, sustainability, and growth. Every day, we challenge the conventional and push the boundaries of what manufacturing can be — for the benefit of people and the planet.

The company language is English, and the position demands strong written and spoken English skills.

The role

This role is key in bridging the gap between R&D and production, ensuring that new products and processes are efficiently industrialized following proof-of-concept validation. The Senior Industrialization Engineer will work closely with R&D, Process Engineering, and Quality Engineering teams to design and implement robust, cost-effective manufacturing solutions.

What You’ll Do

• 
Establish the most efficient way to produce products and processes after proof-of-concept validation.

• 
Collect and analyze data for data driven improvements and decitions.

• 
Design custom machines or tooling according to our production method.

• 
Work closely with R&D, Process Engineering, and Quality Engineering to ensure smooth industrialization.

• 
Actively participate in CAPEX planning and procurement processes for new equipment and tooling, including close contact with suppliers.

• 
Contribute to PFMEA and Control Plan development to ensure quality is built into the process.

• 
Identify opportunities for process optimization and cost reduction while maintaining product integrity.

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for someone who is motivated and enthusiastic about the opportunity to shape industrialization processes from the ground up, bringing valuable experience and insights gained from successfully navigating multiple industrialization and development cycles in previous projects.

You are experienced in a Manufacturing/Production and feel confident entering this role with your existing skillsets and are still hungry for further growth and development.

You find it motivating to be a part of a Company's journey going from startup to scaleup, that offers a different kind of environment than other typical traditional manufacturing companies offer.

Experience matters — but so does attitude and passion.

Qualifications

• 
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related field.

• 
Minimum 5 years of experience in hands on industrialization management or process engineering within manufacturing or automotive sectors.

• 
Great advantage with Lean Six Sigma certification.

• 
Strong understanding of PFMEA, Control Plans, and lean manufacturing principles.

• 
Experience with CAPEX planning and supplier management.

• 
Excellent problem-solving and project management skills.

• 
Strong English communication skills, both written and spoken.

• 
Ability to thrive in a start-up environment with hands-on involvement.

• 
Advantage but not a requirement with experience from either bicycle tire development, injection moulding or RF welding.

Personal Qualities

• 
Proactive and solution-oriented.

• 
Motivated by innovation and fast-changing environments.

• 
Flexible and comfortable working in a modern, small-team environment with real influence.

• 
Precise, organized, structured and good work ethics.

• 
Good communication skills.

• 
Independent and self-driven.

• 
A positive team player who contributes to a great work culture.

Why Work at reTyre?

🌱 Be a Pioneer — Join a company redefining an entire industry

🚀 Real Impact — Your ideas can become reality fast

🤝 People First Culture — We invest in our team through collaboration, support, and growth

🧠 Innovation Every Day — Work with motivated experts shaping the future

💼 Competitive Salary & Benefits

🚗 Easy Work-Life Balance — Traffic-free commute to Ski, free parking, charging stations

Will You Help Us Bring the Future to the Table?
We think you might.

If you’re hungry to make an impact- to move quickly, build smart, and help shape the future of an entire industry- you might be exactly who we’re looking for.

At Munu, we’re on a mission to transform how restaurants and bars run, grow, and thrive. We blend a deep love for food and tech with bold ambition — creating tools that simplify operations, elevate guest experiences, and empower hospitality teams to perform at their best.

We move fast- and we mean it. We’d rather try something, learn from it, and improve, than sit on the fence for too long. You’ll feel that from day one.

We challenge ideas, not people. We share wins. And because we work directly with restaurants every day, you’ll see the real-world impact of what you build.

If you like what you read, pull up a chair.
About the Role
When a venue’s tills stop, the evening doesn’t wait. As a Helpdesk Agent at Munu, you’re the first voice restaurants and bars hear when something isn’t working, and your job is to get them back to trading, fast.

You’ll handle first-line calls, tickets and chats from venues across Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland. You’ll solve what can be solved at first contact, escalate cleanly what can’t, and help reduce how many problems reach us in the first place.

You’ll work closely with our Product Support & Quality Specialists, who pick up your escalations; our Account Managers, whose customers you’re helping; and our Hardware & Logistics Specialist, on hardware faults and replacements.
Your Mission, Should You Choose to Accept It
• 
Answer and resolve first-line calls, tickets and chats from venues across our Nordic markets, getting it right at first contact wherever you can.

• 
Get to the real problem: establish what’s happening, how urgent it is for the customer’s service, and whether first line can fix it.

• 
Escalate a diagnosed problem, along with what you’ve already tried, rather than a forwarded message, and raise potential major incidents to the Helpdesk Manager without delay.

• 
Keep customers informed while an issue is being resolved by someone else.

• 
Help reduce what arrives: guide customers to our self-service and help content, and flag recurring questions and missing or incorrect help content, with evidence, to our specialists and Product Managers.

• 
Keep accurate ticket records in Zendesk and make handovers easy for colleagues to pick up.

• 
Work to a rota that follows the hours venues trade, which may include shifts outside normal office hours, plus occasional travel for team gatherings, training and venue visits.
You’ll Thrive in This Role If You…
• 
Stay calm and friendly with a customer whose venue can’t trade.

• 
Ask the right questions to find the real problem before acting.

• 
Own a case until it’s resolved or cleanly handed over.

• 
Write clear, accurate notes that a colleague can pick up without asking.

• 
Have experience in customer support or customer service (for example first-line support, retail or hospitality), including troubleshooting technical or operational problems for customers under time pressure.

• 
Have completed upper secondary education or a trade certificate, or at least 2 years of experience in customer service, customer support or hospitality.

• 
Have experience with at least one of: supporting customers by phone, ticket or chat; POS or other systems used in restaurants and bars; hardware such as payment terminals, printers, kitchen displays or in-venue networks; or onboarding and training customers on new systems.

• 
Communicate professionally in English, spoken and written. You’ll work across every function and with customers in several countries.

• 
Use approved AI tools in your daily work, check what they produce, and protect customer data.

Bonus points if you…

• 
Have worked in hospitality operations, such as a restaurant, bar or hotel.

• 
Have experience with POS or payment systems.

• 
Speak Norwegian and more than one Scandinavian language, since contacts come from venues across the Nordics.

• 
Have used Zendesk or a similar ticketing system.

• 
Have spotted recurring issues or gaps in help content and done something about it.

• 
Have built an AI-supported routine or tool that colleagues use.
What Success Looks Like
• 
Most of your contacts are resolved at first line, and they stay resolved.

• 
Customers get answers quickly, and they rate your service well. Speed only counts when customers are served well.

• 
Your escalations are accepted by second line first time, with nothing missing.

• 
Recurring questions get fewer, because customers know where to find help and gaps in help content get fixed.
What Makes This Opportunity Different
• 
You’ll grow with us. This role has real room to develop- into product support, implementation, or hardware and logistics, or towards handling our most complex contacts and helping train colleagues. You don’t need to have it all figured out from day one; we’ll help you get there.

• 
You’ll be part of a company with deep industry knowledge and a mission that matters- empowering hospitality teams with better tools.

• 
You’ll shape how a core business function is built- not just follow a playbook. We’re at a stage where your input genuinely changes how things work.

• 
You’ll work with smart, kind, ambitious people across the Nordics- the kind who disagree openly, share the credit, and don’t take themselves too seriously.

• 
You’ll have the freedom to test, fail, learn, and try again- with the support and tools to do your best work.
Who We Are
Munu is a Norwegian scale-up rethinking how restaurants and bars operate- and thrive. Since 2016, we’ve helped over 2,000 hospitality venues run smarter with our Munu Cloud platform, integrating everything from POS and Booking to Inventory and Payments. Our customers range from local gems to national brands, and our reach is growing fast across the Nordics.

Backed by strong investors and built by a team that lives and breathes hospitality, we’re committed to growing sustainably- without compromising trust, creativity, or simplicity. The best part? You’ll see the results of your work in the real world- in the restaurants and bars people actually love.

At Munu, we empower our customers- and we empower our people. How we work matters just as much as what we achieve. Michelin-star ambition, kitchen-team spirit. We move fast and hold high standards, but we also give feedback with care, celebrate each other’s wins, and make sure the best idea wins regardless of where it comes from.

If you’re curious about joining us, take a moment to read our Cultural Principles before you apply. They’ll give you a sense of who we are and the kind of culture you’ll be part of. Sound like the kind of place you’d do your best work? We’d love to hear from you.

Let’s bring the future to the table, together.

Qualifications

• 

Practical understanding of web applications (SaaS), mobile app sync, and how software runs in production.

• 

Comfortable using application telemetry, monitoring, or server logs to validate your hypotheses efficiently without getting lost in the data.

• 

Strong communication skills in Norwegian and English, with a knack for explaining technical topics simply.

• 

Experience from 2nd-line technical support, IT operations, or QA is an advantage.

• 

Skilled at taking vague user symptoms, deducing the underlying conditions, and attempting to reproduce or isolate the failure domain systematically without needing direct code access.

Candidates must pass a pre-employment background check (bakgrunnssjekk ) and meet the conduct requirements (krav til vandel/politiattest) for aviation background checks (Luftfartstilsynet) and/or customer-mandated security clearances.

Pedagogical: You enjoy talking to users and teaching others how a system works.

Structured: You keep tickets tidy, respect security standards, and follow issues through to resolution.

Debug & Troubleshoot: Analyze customer tickets and server/application logs to pinpoint root causes and resolve issues directly.

A key operational role in an international aviation tech company headquartered at Bodø Airport.

Career growth paths toward DevOps, technical customer success, or product management.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

At Lys Bemanning AS, we assist clients with recruitment and staffing, and we are always looking for the best candidates. Although we recruit personnel for all industries, our core business is focused on engineers and skilled workers.

About Nordscale
Nordscale is the specialist operator for mission-critical AI data centers. We manage the operations that keep AI compute sites running reliably, efficiently, and safely. Founded as a strategic partnership between the AI hyperscaler Nscale and Norwegian energy company Nordkraft, we harness local expertise and data center operations experience to deliver service excellence to our customers, while building skilled local jobs and partnering with Norwegian businesses to create lasting value in the regions where we work.

 

Our culture combines local Northern Norwegian values, international expertise, and disciplined operational excellence. We’re a team built on trust, ownership, and collaboration: we communicate openly, take accountability for outcomes, and work as one team across sites, partners, and functions to deliver performance people can depend on.

 
About the Role (Job Purpose)
As Facility Director, you will lead Nordscale’s Facility Management unit at Kvandal South outside Narvik, one of the largest AI data-centre projects in Europe. You will be central in building the  unit ahead of and during the start of operations. You will hold overall responsibility for safe and stable operation of the facility, the buildings and the services around them, around the clock.

 

You will report to the Site Director and lead managers within quality, HSE, site coordination and logistics, sustainability and technical operations. 

 
What You’ll be Doing (Responsibilities)
• Recruit and build the Facility Management unit, and prepare the organisation, procedures and suppliers for the start of operations in 2027.
• Hold overall responsibility for safe, stable and efficient 24/7 operation of the facility. This includes building and site services such as property management, security, logistics, spare parts and sustainability.
• Own the operational management system, including KPIs, meeting structure, reporting and follow-up. Build a strong safety and quality culture with strict operational discipline, and act as Incident Commander during major incidents.
• Work closely with the Site Director, Nscale and IT teams. Manage supplier performance and budgets for maintenance, upgrades, energy and technical services. 
 
About You (Skills, Qualifications & Experience)
 You may be an experienced leader from data centres. You may also come from other technically complex, continuous operations where downtime has major consequences, such as process industry, metallurgy, pulp and paper, offshore, maritime operations, power or technical defence environments. Experience from establishing an operating organisation before a facility enters regular operation is an advantage. 

You are motivated by building something from the ground up, and you combine trust with clear follow-up. You know that following the standard and improving it are equally important parts of the same responsibility.

 

Key characteristics

•  Structured and systematic, working with strong procedural discipline and attention to detail.
• Resilient under pressure, identifying challenges and finding pragmatic, holistic solutions.
• Builds relationships of trust, collaboration and mutual respect, communicates clearly and listens actively.
 

Skills & Qualifications 

•  Solid experience leading managers across several technical disciplines and support functions in 24/7 operations, together with subcontractors.
• A strong track record in safety culture and HSE, including work and access permits, safe isolation, risk assessment and change management.
• Experience with establishing and leading a performance management system, policies and procedures (SOPs etc) and supplier follow-up
• Sound understanding of electrical, cooling and mechanical systems.
• Experience from commissioning and start-up is an advantage.
• Fluent English and a Scandinavian language, written and spoken. 
• A master’s degree in electrical, mechanical or automation engineering is preferred. Other relevant technical education combined with documented operational experience will also be considered. What We Can Offer You
• Competitive salary negotiable based on experience. 
• Performance-based bonus tied to results and company performance. 
• The chance to build the operating organisation, procedures and safety culture from the ground up, and to lead Kvandal South into operation in 2027.
• Relocation support assessed individually, if required.  Equal Opportunities Statement
We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities.  We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

 

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Intelligent Navigation and Risk Based Route Planning
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The PhD position is part of the Norwegian Maritime AI Centre, led by NTNU. The centre brings together researchers, industry and public partners to develop AI applications for the maritime sector. 

The PhD project will develop AI methods for navigational situational awareness and risk-based route planning, with applications in safe navigation and wind-assisted propulsion. A key question is how maritime data can be used to assess navigational risk and inform route and speed choices, accounting for vessel capabilities and uncertainty in the available information. 

The work will draw on two of the center's use cases: AI-driven S-100 electronic navigational chart products (UC3) and wind-assisted propulsion (UC5).

UC3 concerns the use of electronic navigational chart data to assess hazards along a vessel’s path. The use case will investigate how these assessments can account for the vessel’s position and motion, together with characteristics such as draught, stopping distance and maneuvering capabilities. Historical AIS tracks combined with chart data offer a basis for constructing and studying navigational situations. It is also a goal of the use case that these assessments should be explainable. That is, it should be possible to trace a warning or recommendation to the data and criteria that produced it.

In UC5, the focus is on route and speed planning for vessels with wind-assisted propulsion. Taking advantage of wind conditions can reduce fuel consumption, but the benefits depend on the vessel’s performance and the route it can safely follow. The use case will investigate both how forecasts of wind and other environmental conditions can be used in voyage planning, accounting for navigational and operational constraint, and how adaptations can be made underway, accounting for actual conditions. 

The two use cases link the assessment of individual navigational situations to planning over a longer voyage. The project will examine how uncertainty in data and forecasts affects these decisions, and how plans can be revised as conditions change. Method development will build on machine learning in combination with established models of vessel behavior and navigation. The choice of methods will be developed as part of the doctoral work.

The candidate will work closely with industry and public partners in the centre.

The PhD candidate will be supervised by Associate Professor Børge Rokseth.
About the project
DThe Norwegian Maritime AI Centre shall position the maritime sector for accelerated and successful use of AI. The demand for safe and sustainable maritime activities, as well as the shortage of crew and engineers, are key drivers for change in the maritime sector. At the same time, there is a pull for growth, increased efficiency and profitability, while managing volatility in the markets. Moreover, the sector is critically important for global supply chains and security in a tense geopolitical situation. To demonstrate and prototype maritime AI solutions, the center will address a diverse and impactful set of use cases: Logistics, shipping and business transactions; Ship design and construction; Voyage planning and optimization; Condition monitoring and maintenance; Crew training; Maritime traffic and ship surveillance; Decarbonization and energy management; Autonomous ships and remote control. 

The research partners are the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), University of Oslo, Oslo School of Architecture and Design, Royal Norwegian Naval Academy, Norwegian Mapping Authority, MET and SINTEF Nordvest. There are about 30 user partners from the maritime sector, in addition to hundreds of members of the Maritime Forum, Blue Maritime, Ocean Autonomy, and Maritime CleanTech clusters. The center will be a hub, orchestrating the interfaces with research partners and user partners to facilitate collaboration, knowledge creation, dissemination, innovation, and sharing of knowledge. The Norwegian Maritime AI Center is funded by the Research Council of Norway and the partners for the period 2026-2030. There will be approximately 25 doctoral scholarships and some postdoc positions. More information can be found here: https://www.ntnu.edu/mai 
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the Norwegian Maritime AI Centre activities 
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Other career-promoting work can be discussed and agreed
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a strong foundation in engineering cybernetics, including mathematical modelling, dynamical systems and control theory, together with competence in machine learning. This background must be documented through relevant coursework and project or thesis work.
• You must have good programming skills and experience implementing and evaluating mathematical models or computational methods in Python, MATLAB, C++ or a comparable programming language.
• You must have a Master's degree in engineering cybernetics, robotics, control engineering, applied mathematics, or another closely related discipline. Applicants with degrees in other engineering disciplines or informatics must document an equivalent background in the subjects specified above. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, including 120 credits at master's level. Master's students may apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If your previous studies were not assessed using letter grades, you must demonstrate an equally strong academic foundation. Applicants with a weaker grade background may be considered if they can document that they are particularly suitable for PhD education.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the PhD program in Engineering Cybernetics.
• You must have good written and oral English language skills. If your native language is not English or a Scandinavian language, you must document your English proficiency, for example through TOEFL. 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Knowledge of maritime navigation, vessel dynamics or maritime risk assessment.
• Experience with simulation-based evaluation, uncertainty modelling or risk-based decision-making.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work in interdisciplinary teams with researchers, industry and government.
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Take initiative and work independently when needed
• Contribute to a positive, inclusive and collaborative working environment
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• working capital that can be used to implement the project
• mentor program as a new employee at NTNU
• training during working hours and company sports at NTNU
• As a public employee, you have favourable benefits as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)  Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be from NOK 580 000 NOK per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD program in Engineering Cybernetics within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral program through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• CV 
• Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of minimum two relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Associate Professor Børge Rokseth, email: borge.rokseth@ntnu.no . 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Consultant Berit Dahl, e-mail: berit.dahl@ntnu.no .

Application deadline: 01.12.2026.

For practical information about working at NTNU, please visit this webpage.

About the position
We invite applicants for a full-time position as a PhD research fellow at the Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. The position is associated with the Personality unit at the Section for Health, Developmental, and Personality Psychology (HUP). The PhD will focus on development of personality and depression across the lifespan, and will be connected to The Depression Research Initiative (DRIVE) at the Department of Psychology. 
 
The appointment is a fulltime position for a period of three years. The employment period can be up to 4 years given addition of teaching and administrative duties, depending on the competence of the successful applicant and the resources and needs of the Department of Psychology.

Start date: Spring 2027.
More about the position
The PhD candidate will be part of the Personality group and focus on the relationship between personality, depression, and other mental health conditions. Personality is important for the development and course of mental health problems, and may affect how environmental risk factors affect mental health, as well as the consequences of mental health problems for social and academic functioning. The PhD project will be part of The Depression Research Initiative (DRIVE), made up by five work packages https://www.sv.uio.no/psi/english/research/groups/drive/index.html. 

The key objective of DRIVE is to encompass several core aspects of depression research, so they collectively can address questions that cannot be managed by a single work package. The current position will be related to the work package focusing on development of depression. The PhD project will answer some of the following overarching research questions, with a focus on depression: 

• How do characteristics of the individual and the environment predict personality development?
• What are the associations between personality traits and mental health outcomes, including depression, personal relationships, and work and academic functioning?
• What are the associations between characteristics of parents and children regarding personality and mental health, including depression?Your main tasks will be
• Contributing to developing more specific research questions within the project.
• Complete a PhD thesis in Psychology.
• Publish research papers in international scientific journals.
• Provide scientific presentations to an international audience.
• Participate in the PhD program at the Department of Psychology.Qualifications
Required skills

• At the time of the application, the applicants must have obtained a Cand. Psychol. degree, or a Master’s degree in psychology or a closely related field.
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English are required.
• Experience in conducting statistical analyses.
• A strong interest in the topic of the PhD position.
• Interest in finding and reading relevant literature, defining research questions, preparing and analyzing data, and writing manuscripts.
To be employed as a PhD Research Fellow at the Department of Psychology, applicants must meet the admission requirements for the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences, with specialisation in Psychology. The successful candidate will be admitted to this programme option, subject to approval of the individual project proposal. Please see the Faculty’s admission requirements and the structure of the Psychology programme option.
 
Preferred skills

• Experience with running statistical analyses in R.
• Knowledge of personality, developmental psychology, and/or depression.
• Good writtenand oral proficiency inNorwegian.
• Experience with analyzing longitudinal data.
• Experience with conducting literature reviews.
• Previous research and interest in the above-mentioned topics. 
• Proven ability to work independently and efficiently on relevant research topics.Personal skills
• Ability to work independently and to collaborate effectively with others.
• Curiosity and interest in learning.
• Strong motivation and organizational skills. 
• Ability to think creatively within a scientific framework.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.

The Department of Psychology is one of seven units of the Faculty of Social Sciences, and has 75 permanent and 70 temporary members of scientific staff. Degrees are offered at bachelor and master level, plus a clinical training programme, and the PhD programme has 140 students.
